findings.location: docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/acceptance.md ### S3, the row bound to crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature :: Remove says how many workspaces stop posting, and reading it removes nothing (handoff.json acceptance.S3 row 2, obligations L6/F203)
findings.obligation: L6/F203: GET the remove door twice with a saved app leaves the row, the activity list and the configuration version exactly as they were (P4: the remove page changes nothing, including when prefetched)
findings.observation: The configuration-version clause has no observation anywhere in the slice. The one cited test is the public scenario, whose closing step then_saved_app_unchanged (crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs:1564) observes the page still reading 'Slack: set up here, app ...', both secrets set, no 'replaced the Slack app' activity line, Add to Slack still targeting the app, and an event signed with the saved secret still verifying - it never reads the config version, and a version bumped by a read is invisible on those surfaces. In this same commit the only test that could have reached it, the S2 row 'the table of what the confirm and remove pages reach when they are only read', was narrowed to the confirm page (facts F558/F560) and now cites only L6/F201 and L6/F202, while its locator text still names 'the confirm and remove pages'. So a GET handler that reached a version-bumping write would pass every cited observation.
findings.remediation: Cite L6/F203 at a crafter-authored handler table that covers the remove door's GET - either extend the existing S3 row 'crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs :: the table of the controls the page offers over each app in effect' and its declared stimulus, or add one row for the read-only doors of this slice, and align the S2 locator text with the confirm-only scope it now declares. If the version clause is not meant to be observable at this slice, return F203 to the design owner for restatement rather than leaving it cited but unobserved.

findings.location: docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/acceptance.md ### S3, the row bound to crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature :: Once the Slack app is removed no replica accepts Slack's events any more (handoff.json acceptance.S3 row 7, obligations L9/F217)
findings.obligation: The recorded stimulus of an acceptance row is the state its test constructs, so that a later reader and the examiner judge the same situation
findings.observation: The row's stimulus reads 'This Foundry runs as two replicas on one database with a workspace connected, and the instance admin removes the Slack app.', but the scenario constructs no connected workspace: its Givens are 'this Foundry runs as two replicas with its instance key set by the operator', 'Priya has generated the secrets key' and 'every replica has the Slack app 6123456789012.7234567890123 in effect', with no 'Priya has connected Canzan Labs to Slack with this Foundry's app' step. The scenario therefore also exercises the n = 0 remove page rather than the n = 1 one the stimulus implies. L9/F217 itself ('both replicas answer 401 to an event signed with the removed secret') is fully observed by then_no_replica_verifies, which asks each replica at its own address under the 60 s bound, so no law observation is lost.
findings.remediation: Make the two agree: either add 'Priya has connected Canzan Labs to Slack with this Foundry''s app' to that scenario, which also makes the replica removal happen with something to preserve, or correct the row's stimulus text to say that no workspace is connected.

observations.text: RED reuse, no new execution: tree clean at 2f9d415 (git status --porcelain empty), and the oracle plus supports named by the bundle are exactly the bytes of that commit, so the run recorded at revision 2f9d415 in ~/.cache/nwdes/iis-slack-replace-remove/s3-red.txt is the evidence for this review. That run reports '29 scenarios (20 passed, 9 failed)', '341 steps (332 passed, 9 failed)', 'acceptance run failed: 9 step(s) failed, 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)', exit via 'error: test failed, to rerun pass -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance'. I executed no cargo or lane command in this review; the selection I ran was static (git show of 2f9d415 over the three oracle/support paths, grep over crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps, python step-regex matching), all exit 0.

Step closure checked mechanically, because RED skips every Then after the first failure and so cannot witness them: 3083 step patterns were collected from crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/*.rs and matched against the 40 distinct step phrases of the 9 new scenarios. Every phrase matches exactly one definition - none undefined, none ambiguous. The phrases borrowed from other features resolve too: 'the workspace integrations page reads' at feature_external_integration_plugins.rs:648, 'Lena''s route to ... reads a status starting' at :394, 'the history of the route to ... still lists' at :552, and the connection/email step at feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:451 delegating to eip::then_not_lost (external_integration_plugins.rs:5400, which also asserts zero 'lost its Slack connection' emails in the mail double).

The declared pre-existing bindings resolve and really observe their case. The named tests all exist: a_value_is_judged_the_same_with_surrounding_whitespace, any_32_lowercase_hex_is_accepted_as_a_secret, a_character_outside_the_alphabet_is_refused_as_malformed and a_save_is_refused_on_the_first_blank_or_malformed_field_in_form_order in crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/slack_app.rs, and slack_save_fences_on_the_sealing_key in crates/foundry-store/tests/iis_instance_store.rs. L2/F172 is the 32-lowercase-hex property asserting both secret fields accept and the whole form refuses nothing (slack_app.rs:626); L2/F175 is the outside-alphabet property with prop_assume on non-whitespace asserting Malformed of that same field (:635), matching 'never as blank'; L2/F171, F173 and F174 are rows of the 14-row form-order table (:565) - blank, '   ', uppercase secret, '1.2.3' and the dotless ID among them.

The two edits the root flagged check out. The S1 L2 row's locator is now crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/slack_app.rs::a_value_is_judged_the_same_with_surrounding_whitespace, which exists at that path. The S2 read-only-doors row is genuinely narrowed: its stimulus now reads 'The confirm page is opened, with a submission waiting and with none.' and its user result names only the confirm page (facts F558/F560 replacing F554/F556), and it keeps only L6/F201 and L6/F202. The narrowing is right for S2, where the remove door does not exist - but see finding 1 for what it leaves uncovered in S3.

Test-time budget: no finding. The oracle adds no statement or measurement of per-test time, and nothing in the reviewed bytes sits at or above half a budget in a way that would call for the nine-run median evidence; the two new 60-second observations (then_no_replica_verifies and the existing replica steps) advance the injected fake clock and poll, as the shipped replica scenarios already do.

diagnostic: Accepted. The S3 public oracle is constructible, independent and complete for P4, P5, P6 and P7, and its missing behaviour has a semantic RED. Nine scenarios drive the production router in process at the real public doors (the instance page's Replace and Remove controls, GET and POST of /admin/instance/integrations/slack/remove with the page's own CSRF token) and assert only shipped artefacts: the locked I-15 copy in both count forms, the one Remove control, no key or secret on the page, I-16, the I-18 removed line in an exact ordered activity list, W-2 on the workspace page, the connection not lost and no email in the mail double, the route still retrying with AUTH-12 in its history, re-saving finding Canzan Labs still connected, 401 from each replica asked directly within 60 s, and both the withheld controls and the refused POST under the environment's app. The recorded RED at this same commit is semantic throughout - 404 on the remove door for seven scenarios, an instance page with no Replace or Remove control for two - with 0 parsing and 0 hook errors and the 20 S1/S2 scenarios still passing; I reused that run rather than claim a new one, the tree being clean and the oracle bytes identical. Because RED skips the Thens after a failure, I checked step closure mechanically instead: all 40 distinct step phrases of the new scenarios match exactly one of the 3083 collected definitions, none undefined and none ambiguous. Case closure is total: every finite case of L1 to L11 plus T1 and T2 is cited, L2 keeps its properties, and the cells bound to tables that do not exist yet are honestly declared completion obligations. Both flagged edits are sound: the S1 L2 locator now names a test that exists, and the S2 read-only row is really narrowed to the confirm page. Two non-blocking oracle findings stay open for the ATD and do not veto craft: L6/F203's configuration-version clause lost its only possible witness when the S2 row was narrowed, so a read that bumped the version would pass every cited observation; and the replica-removal row's stimulus claims a connected workspace its scenario never connects. Neither loses a promised user outcome, and both must be closed before completion. No design, implementation or product finding.
